subject: industrial-systems
audience: FE Industrial & Systems candidates and industrial engineering students
title: The Part That Lost $45, Not $60
featured_title: THE PART THAT LOST 45 DOLLARS NOT 60

presentation.challenge: Quality loss did not grow linearly with deviation from target. Under the Taguchi quadratic model, a 3-unit deviation caused a $45 loss.

practice.primary_question: How is quality loss calculated using the Taguchi quadratic loss function?
practice.typical_exam_trap: Assuming quality loss is linearly proportional to deviation from target rather than proportional to the square of the deviation.

case_dna.target_misconception: If a 4-unit deviation causes an $80 loss, a 3-unit deviation causes 3/4 of that loss, or $60.
case_dna.why_plausible: Linear interpolation is intuitive, but the Taguchi model specifies a quadratic relationship.
case_dna.contradicting_evidence: L=k(y-T)^2. From 80=k(4)^2, k=5 dollars/unit². At a 3-unit deviation, L=5(3)^2=$45.
case_dna.corrected_model: Determine k from a known loss-deviation pair, then apply the quadratic Taguchi loss function L=k(y-T)^2.

problem_statement: A quality characteristic has target T=100 units. A deviation of 4 units from target is associated with an $80 quality loss. Assume the Taguchi loss function L=k(y-T)^2. A produced part measures y=103. A note scales the $80 loss linearly by 3/4 and reports $60. Determine the correct loss.

gates.label: Incident
gates.heading: The loss coefficient was hidden inside a quadratic model.
gates.prompt: What exponent applies to the deviation in the Taguchi model?

options.label: Use L=k(y-T)^2
options.reason: This is the stated Taguchi quadratic loss function.

options.label: Use the same $80 loss for any off-target part
options.reason: The loss changes with deviation magnitude.

gates.label: Predict
gates.heading: Predict the loss for y=103
gates.prompt: Enter the quality loss in dollars.

gates.label: Gap
gates.heading: Prove the loss
gates.prompt: First find k=80/4², then calculate k(3²). Enter dollars.
gates.hint: The deviation is 103-100=3, and it must be squared.

gates.label: Evidence
gates.heading: Quadratic loss changes faster than linear intuition

gates.label: Redline
gates.heading: Correct the quality-cost note
report: C1. A 4-unit deviation corresponds to an $80 loss.
C2. The new deviation is 3 units.

claims.label: C1
claims.reason: This is the calibration point given in the problem.

claims.label: C2
claims.reason: The new deviation magnitude is correct.

claims.label: C3
claims.reason: It assumes linear rather than quadratic loss.

evidence_choices.label: k=5 and L=5(3²)=$45
evidence_choices.reason: This follows the stated Taguchi loss function.

correction.template: The Taguchi quality loss for the 103-unit part is ${loss}.

gates.label: Design Fix
gates.heading: Keep expected loss at or below $20 per part

options.label: Hold deviation to 2 units or less

gates.label: Transfer
gates.heading: Apply the loss function to another deviation
gates.prompt: With the same k, what is the loss at |y-T|=2.5?

options.reason: That would come from a linear scaling rule.
That multiplies k by deviation without squaring.

gates.explanation: Taguchi loss grows with the square of deviation from target.

gates.label: Sign Off
gates.heading: Sign off the quality-loss calculation
gates.confirmation: I confirm that the stated Taguchi model is quadratic in deviation from target and should not be scaled linearly.

items.label: What failed
items.value: Loss was interpolated linearly from the calibration point.

items.label: What was missed
items.value: The Taguchi function squares the deviation from target.

items.label: Corrected model
items.value: Use L=k(y-T)^2 after determining k from the given loss condition.

seo.seo_title: Taguchi Quality Loss Function Calculation | FE Industrial E-089
seo.meta_description: Solve FE Industrial & Systems Case E-089: if a 4-unit deviation costs $80, then k=5 and a 3-unit deviation causes a $45 Taguchi loss.
seo.focus_keyphrase: FE Industrial Taguchi quality loss function
seo.excerpt: Taguchi quality loss is quadratic, not linear, in deviation from target.
seo.direct_answer: From $80=k(4²), k=$5 per squared unit. At y=103 with target 100, deviation is 3, so L=5(3²)=$45.

faqs.q: What is the Taguchi loss function?
faqs.a: L=k(y-T)^2 for the quadratic model used here.

faqs.q: What deviation keeps loss at or below $20 when k=5?
faqs.a: A deviation of 2 units or less.
